candidates.title: Show HN: Stop applying to jobs using AI-generated resume
candidates.raw_content: When LLMs hands you a resume or pdf it carry markers of how it was made, including the source. You can't see them on the page but applicant tracking systems can read it. So recruiters are flagging such profiles and rejecting them entirely. I had tested this across 40+ AI models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, etc) to produce a resume and every single file carried a marker. To solve this problem. I had built a free tool to show what your file says and gives you a cleaned version: - Drop your resume and get a cleaned copy - Free, no account. What it doesn't do: it won't rewrite your resume or make AI-sounding wording more human. It only deals with what's hidden in the file. It's a simple tool, but it feels absolutely necessary now as more people are using AI for generating their entire resume or even editing them. I am the developer, happy to answer any questions. candidates.title: This year we’ve had a clear jump in model capability where instead of telling agents precisely what to do, it’s better to use these systems to solve problems you can’t easily define yourself. A year ago you’d need to very clearly tell agents the how to design and develop your product idea, or there was almost no chance of success. Now, increasingly, the agent likely can come up with a better implementation than you’d have thought of because you can have it connect the dots between a far greater solution space than you can. This will be increasingly true in basically every domain of kneeler work. We’re going to see this impact in finance, legal, life sciences, cyber, and many other spaces where no person can hold onto all the available relevant industry knowledge to think of the best solution. Ultimately this is going to reshape our relationship with AI and how we deploy agents in our work. It won’t be about explicitly telling them, but instead giving them goals and enough freedom to pursue them in the best way they can.
